extracted.intended_audience: chemical indexers and patent information specialists (Derwent/chemical patent indexing)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and coding guidelines for assigning chemical index codes (Parts A–G, C0–C8, ring codes, RINs, substituents, etc.) to chemical structures disclosed in patent documents. Covers element presence, valency, inorganic vs organic treatment, ring-system coding, spiro and substituent rules, and Ring Index Number usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Z-atom functional-group coding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional group and element (Z atom) coding depends on the identity of Z, its valency, and the bonds it forms (e.g. Z-O, Z-S, Z-N, Z-C); specific code sets and combinations are assigned according to these bonding patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page illustrate numerous permutations (P, As, B etc.) where the number and type of Z–X bonds, valency (e.g. trivalent P), and total number of Z atoms in the compound determine which B/other codes are assigned. Follow the explicit element-specific definitions and note exceptions (e.g. when Parts H–L codes are not used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phosphorus coding in aliphatic compounds (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phosphorus in an aliphatic compound is coded according to number of Z–O bonds, presence/absence of Z–S bonds, trivalent/pentavalent state, and the total number of Z atoms in the compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Three or more Z–O bonds; No Z to S bonds; Trivalent P; Total of one Z atom in the compound' (use appropriate B-codes listed). Also illustrated are variants with two Z–O bonds plus one Z–N bond, peroxide relationships, and ketal O–C–O patterns; assign the specific code combination matching the bonding pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element-specific examples used as coding templates (P, As, B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific example fragments (e.g. As in a carbocyclic compound, B in a carbocyclic compound) have precise coding requirements such as 'one Z to O bond; no Z to S bonds; two Z to C bonds; trivalent As; one Z atom' or 'three or more Z to C bonds; trivalent B'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When patent text or structure matches one of these example fragments, apply the listed set of codes (the guide lists explicit B- and J-codes). These examples serve as templates for similar structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical treatment of acyl chlorides (-C(=O)-Cl)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cl in -C(=O)-Cl is identified differently depending on date: used to identify Cl in -C(=O)-Cl from 1978 forward; treated as parent acid prior to 1978.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When indexing records from 1978 onward, include the C0 halogen code to identify Cl in acyl chlorides; for pre‑1978 records, do not code Cl this way (treat as parent acid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Note B840 (Z as ring heteroatom) not coded
rubrics_metrics.description: B840 ('Z as ring heteroatom in an organic compound') is not coded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assign B840 despite ring heteroatom occurrences; use alternative codes and RINs as appropriate for ring heteroatoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part C scope: inorganic-focused codes and limited organic exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Part C codes cover halogen, H, C, N, O, and S in inorganic compounds, ions, or ligands; Part C codes are not assigned to organic compounds except for the special cases listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign Part C codes to inorganic compounds and to the specific special-case organic situations enumerated in the chapter. See the 'Part C: codes are not assigned to organic compounds, ions, or ligands, other than the special cases listed above.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity dates and applicability of Part C codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified, Part C codes are valid from 1963; sets C1 (except C116), C2, C3, C4, C6 and C8 (except C811 and C812) are valid from 1970; many C1–C4/C6/C8 codes are not valid for natural products before 1981.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the date-validity notes before assigning codes; some codes only apply from particular years forward and some are restricted for natural products.

rubrics_metrics.name: C0: identification of halogens present (and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set C0 identifies halogen atoms (unspecified halogen, F, Cl, Br, I) present in compounds, with specific usage exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use C0 codes for halogens in inorganic compounds, halogens as ring heteroatoms, and certain other cases; exceptions include: C0 codes assigned only after 1978 for halogens in compounds with Z atoms; not used for halogens that are part of ions containing a metal atom (e.g. PtCl6); halogens bonded to heteroatoms or to -C(=O)- or -C(=S)- in organic compounds are coded instead by functional-group codes (L511/L512 or K1) with the X atom identified by a C0 code (from 1978 forward). Astatine is not in C0 but coded A885.

rubrics_metrics.name: C1: presence of lower-valency halogen, H, C, N, O, or S
rubrics_metrics.description: C1 codes identify halogen valency I or II, hydrogen (excluding NH3+ and including NH4+), carbon, nitrogen with valency II–IV (excluding NH3+/NH4+), oxygen (excluding -O-O-), and sulfur with valency II or III.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the specific C1 subcodes (C100, C101, C106, C107, C108, C116) as applicable. Note cross-assignments with Se/Te where many S codes are also used.

rubrics_metrics.name: C2 and C3: intermediate- and high-valency halogen/N/S
rubrics_metrics.description: C2 codes cover intermediate-valency halogen (III or IV) and S(IV or V); C3 codes cover high-valency halogen (V or more), N (valency V, excluding NH3/NH4+), and S (valency VI or more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use C200–C216 and C300–C316 as appropriate to identify higher oxidation states/valencies in inorganic compounds, ions, or ligands.

rubrics_metrics.name: C4: -O-O- or -S-S- in inorganic compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: C4 identifies peroxy (-O-O-) and disulfide (-S-S-, -S=S-) linkages in inorganic compounds, ions, or ligands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: C408 includes O3 but not O2; when C408 is used, also assign C108 unless a non-peroxy O is present in a separate ion. C416 (S–S) does not include elemental S.

rubrics_metrics.name: C5: inorganic compounds consisting solely of H, C, N, O, and/or S — priority system
rubrics_metrics.description: C5 codes identify inorganic compounds/ions/ligands consisting solely of H, C, N, O and/or S (e.g. NH3/NH4, HNO3/NO3, carbonic acid derivatives, sulphur acids) and follow a priority system where only the first applicable C5 code is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple C5 categories could apply, assign only the first applicable code. Compounds coded in C5 may include other elements only if those elements are present in ions not coded in C5. Elemental N is C520; elemental H and O use C550; elemental C and S are handled via C106/C116 or C810 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: C600: halogen as ring heteroatom usage
rubrics_metrics.description: C600 flags halogen atoms present as ring heteroatoms; the particular halogen is identified with a C0 code and its valency with C100/C200/C300 as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use C600 in combination with the appropriate C0 and valency codes; the guide gives examples showing combinations with L760/K140 etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: C7: descriptors for inorganic compounds/ions without Part B elements
rubrics_metrics.description: C7 codes (C710, C720, C730) denote inorganic cation in an organic compound, inorganic anion in an organic compound, or entirely inorganic compound, and are not used for free elements or ions/compounds containing noble gases, B, Si, P, As, Se, or Te.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply C7 codes when the inorganic part includes Part B elements or noble gases; examples demonstrate FeCl3 as C730 and mixed ionic examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: C8 / C80: elements not present and miscellaneous descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Subset C80 codes indicate elements not present in inorganic compounds/ions/ligands (e.g. metals, noble gases, halogens not present, H not present, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C80 is not applicable to free elements or some mixtures or where the only inorganic part is a metal cation or NH4. Elements present in organic groups of ionic/coordination compounds are considered absent if not present in any inorganic groups. Examples illustrate typical assignments (Na2CO3 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: C81: free element, radioactive element, and specific isotope coding
rubrics_metrics.description: C810 denotes a free element, C811 a radioactive element, and C812 a specific non-radioactive isotope; elements coded in C81 are additionally assigned codes identifying them even if part of an organic group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, 14CH3CHO is coded C811 and C106; D2/H examples show combination uses. C810 together with C106 is coded for elemental C including graphite or diamond and for elemental S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rings as primary indexing starting point
rubrics_metrics.description: Rings are usually the largest, most easily identifiable fragments and are a recommended starting point for selecting chemical codes for searching/indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult ring definitions (alicyclic, aromatic, bridged, carbocyclic, fused, heterocyclic, mononuclear, spiro) and then apply appropriate Parts D–G codes. Use ring-system identification to guide downstream substituent/functional-group coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one D–G code for a mononuclear, fused, or bridged ring system
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign only one code from Parts D: through G: to a mononuclear, fused, or bridged ring system of an organic compound; component rings of fused/bridged systems are not searched individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a code covers more than one possible ring system, refine searches with Ring Index Numbers (RINs) where available (codes covering more than one ring system are marked with an asterisk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of unsaturation handling in ring codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Many ring-system codes cover hydrogenated (more saturated) derivatives unless a separate hydrogenated form code is provided; conversely some code sets cover less-saturated derivatives unless a separate less-saturated code exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: F610 defined as oxazole but covers di- and tetrahydrooxazoles; quinoline searched as D621 with di-/polyhydroquinolines as D622; benzene/cyclohexadiene/cyclohexene/cyclohexane use G1x series as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring substituent coding conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring substituent is any atom/group other than H bonded to a ring atom. Indexers attempt to index all specific substitution patterns disclosed for the most important ring system. Substituents generally do not change the ring code unless tautomerism changes ring hydrogenation state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substituent numbers in D0/F0/G0 refer to ring positions bearing substituents, not total substituent count. Use non-specific substitution codes (D010/D020/F010/G001–G003) when general patterns (e.g. 'optionally substituted benzene') are disclosed, while specifically exemplified/claimed patterns receive more specific substitution codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spiro structure coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ring in a spiro structure is coded separately; the spiro system receives one or more spiro codes (D041, F022, G041, G052) depending on ring types and also receives a Ring Index Number (RIN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show combined code sets (e.g. G223, G041, G031) and note that a Poly code is not used merely because a spiro code appears twice; the entire spiro system receives a RIN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rings containing heteroatoms other than O, S, N — adaptation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For rings with Se or Te, replace Se/Te with S and include Se/Te element codes; for metals bonded to two C atoms treat metal as C for ring code but include A922 (metal in ring) and the specific metal Part A code; for other elements replace them with C for ring code and assign the Part B/C element codes (e.g. B840) and code substituents as if bonded to a heterocyclic ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific examples (Se -> D300 + B634, metal -> treat as C but include A922 and applicable Part A code, Si/P/I examples) and remember that the 'Basic Group' code for these rings is M411 (with pre-1970 exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring atoms coded in non-ring parts and functional-group interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: When rings contain elements other than C, O, S, or N, assign both a ring code from Parts D–G and one or more element codes from Parts A–C; if certain atom/bond combinations occur in a ring they may also get a functional-group code from Set L9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign both types of codes to fully represent ring skeleton and unusual in-ring atom chemistry; consult L9 when combined patterns are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steroid nucleus coding exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Compounds containing the cyclopenta(a)phenanthrene ring system (steroid nucleus) are never assigned codes in Parts D–G nor the steroid RIN 04781; instead they are structure-coded in Parts S, T, and U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the steroid nucleus is spiro- or fused-to another ring, assign the RIN for the complete system (and possibly RIN for the ring spiro to the steroid nucleus) but never assign the steroid nucleus RIN itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: General ring codes usage reserved for exhaustive searches
rubrics_metrics.description: General ring codes (e.g. D040, F020, G040) index patents that mention broad types of rings (e.g. 'aryl', 'aromatic heterocyclic ring system') and are recommended only for the most exhaustive searches; do not apply when specific ring systems are disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer specific ring codes (e.g. F431 for pyridine) for routine search/indexing; use general codes only to capture patents that mention broad classes without specifying particular rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring Index Numbers (RINs) assignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: RINs are five-digit numbers assigned to provide specificity where ring codes cover more than one ring system (codes marked with *), rings containing elements other than C/N/O/S, and spiro rings. RINs indicate the skeleton of ring atoms, not substituents or tautomers, and are applied to the search statements with the relevant codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use RINs for ring systems uniquely identified by a single code, for tautomers or different hydrogenation states, or for metals in rings unless the metal is bonded to two ring C atoms. Derwent-generated RINs supplement The Ring Index; historically up to 117 RINs could be assigned to a single patent. When The Ring Index assigns different numbers to tautomers, Derwent applies the lowest assigned ring number to all tautomeric forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts D and E fused ring heterocycle coding hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes in Parts D and E are hierarchical: first digit indicates heteroatom(s) present and number of rings, second digit differentiates ring sizes/heteroatom positions, third digit indicates hydrogenation state (final '0' means all hydrogenation states, '1' fully unsaturated, '2' hydrogenated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to the ring structures specified, each code covers rings with C atoms replaced by heteroatoms other than O/S/N and S replaced by Se/Te where applicable; use the digit schema to select the correct code and consult the 'Ring Code Finder' summaries for set selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes on coding substituents in Parts D and E (component-by-component)
rubrics_metrics.description: When coding substituents in fused-ring heterocyclic systems, component rings are considered separately: each heterocyclic ring with substituents gets a D01 code and each carbocyclic ring with substituents gets a D02 code. The number of ring atoms bearing substituents is the searchable parameter (not relative positions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: D011 = 1 heterocyclic ring atom bears substituent(s) adjacent (alpha) to ring fusion; D012 = 1 heterocyclic ring atom bears substituent(s) not adjacent (beta) to ring fusion; D016 = two or more substituents on same atom; D030 = substitution at ring fusion atom; use Poly codes when a substitution code applies more than once.
